stem: Mazowe Packaging (Private) Limited has 200,000 shares. The founding family owns 150,000 shares. The directors want US\$500,000 to build a new factory and are considering becoming a public limited company and selling new shares to the public.

parts.label: (a)

parts.stem: Explain **one** advantage to the company of becoming a public limited company.

points.description: Identifies, e.g. can raise large capital from the public (1)
Applies: the US\$500,000 for the factory (1)
Effect, e.g. growth without high-interest loans (1)

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Evaluate whether the family should agree to the company becoming a public limited company.

points.description: For: raises the full US\$500,000 without interest payments (1)
For: shares become easy to sell, so the family's wealth is more liquid (1)
Against: family's percentage falls as new shares are issued; could lose majority control (1)
Against: costs of becoming public / published accounts / takeover risk (1)
Considers alternative, e.g. bank loan or selling shares privately (1)
Justified conclusion (1)

answerSpec.modelAnswer: Going public would raise the US\$500,000 without loan interest and make the family's shares easy to sell. But issuing many new shares would cut the family's 75% holding, possibly below half, so they could lose control, and the company would face higher costs, published accounts and takeover risk. If the factory is profitable enough to repay a loan, borrowing or selling a few shares privately keeps control; the family should go public only if they accept sharing control.

explanation: The family owns 75%. Going public raises large capital but dilutes control and adds costs.
hints: What happens to the family's percentage if new shares are sold?

stem: Three friends plan to open a tourist lodge near Victoria Falls. They need US\$150,000. Two of them have savings; the third has hotel experience but no money. They expect to borrow from a bank.

points.description: Owners/shareholders can lose only the amount they invested (1)
Personal possessions are not at risk for the business's debts (1)

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain **two** reasons why a private limited company would suit the three friends.

points.description: Reason 1: limited liability (1)
Applied: a large bank loan / risky tourism business, so personal assets protected (1)
Reason 2: shares can be allotted to reflect contributions / continuity / easier borrowing (1)
Applied: the friend without money can earn shares for his experience; bank deals with a legal entity (1)

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Recommend whether they should form a partnership or a private limited company. Justify your answer.

points.description: Partnership: cheaper and easier to form; accounts private (1)
Partnership: unlimited liability on a large loan is a serious risk (1)
Company: limited liability and continuity suit a large, long-term investment (1)
Company: formation costs and formalities; bank may want personal guarantees (1)
Uses case evidence (US\$150,000, bank loan, tourism risk) (1)
Justified recommendation (1)

answerSpec.modelAnswer: A partnership would be cheap and quick to set up, but with US\$150,000 at stake and a bank loan, unlimited liability would put all three friends' homes at risk if tourism falls. A private limited company costs more to form, and the bank may still ask for guarantees, but it protects their other assets, continues if one leaves and lets them allot shares fairly. They should form a private limited company.

explanation: With large borrowing and a risky market, limited liability is the deciding factor.
hints: How large is the investment and how risky?
What happens to personal assets in each form?
